leads.name: Arbre botella del Botanic II
leads.reason: Only one source found this pass: the official register itself. No independent article, garden-authority page or Wikipedia entry specific to this individual specimen turned up. Species-name ambiguity noted: the Jardi Botanic's own public catalogue page found in this pass describes a 'arbol botella' / Brachychiton DISCOLOR (not populneus) in the same garden, and both species share the Spanish common name 'arbol botella' (bottle tree), so it is unclear whether the register's populneus ID for this exact specimen is correct or whether the web description refers to a different bottle tree in the garden. Needs either a second independent source for this specific register point, or an in-person/photo check of the trunk and leaf shape to resolve the species question before this can be delivered as verified.

leads.name: Palmera Canaria de Gran Via
leads.reason: Register (register_id 716) names it individually and designates it as a natural monument, on the median of Gran Via del Marques del Turia (which carries 79 palms of five species plus 128 plane trees and other formal planting, laid out 1884, landscaped 1907 per a local blog on the avenue's history). Confirmed as a real, mapped, publicly accessible street tree: it is an OSM natural=tree node (id 13092901321, tagged protected=yes, denotation=natural_monument, circumference 2.15m, height 24.4m) at essentially identical coordinates, but that OSM node explicitly carries reg_ref=716, i.e. it is the SAME register entry re-published on OSM rather than an independently sourced confirmation, so it does not count as the second source under the two-independent-sources bar. Searched the city's own protected-trees page (valenciaverde.es, 472 protected trees citywide, 266 monumental palms), local press (actualidadvalencia.com's piece on the 2026 review of 462 monumental/singular trees, which names four Ficus macrophylla on this same avenue but not this palm), a detailed local-history PDF on the avenue's planting (agroicultura.com, too large to search past its images, general context only: avenue design by architect Francisco Mora, 1907), a Valencia history blog, and iNaturalist and Wikimedia Commons geosearches at this exact point: none named this specific palm. Access is not in question (open median of a public avenue), only the second-source bar. Worth a retry via the Generalitat's own catalogue viewer or a direct call to Valencia's press office/ajuntament open-data portal rather than general web search.

leads.name: Ficus de l'Hort de les Camelies
leads.reason: Register (register_id 672) point falls exactly inside the OSM-mapped 'Hort de les Camelies' (alt_name 'Parque de las Camelias') garden polygon (way 23413077, checked by point-in-polygon), a small public neighbourhood garden in the Aiora/Ayora district of Valencia, tagged with no fee and independently confirmed as a real, public, free municipal garden by a January 2024 citizen-journalism article (noticiasciudadanas.com) describing its (poor) maintenance state, run by the city's Parks and Gardens department. That article does not name or describe the ficus itself, only a weevil-infested palm in the same garden, so it corroborates the LOCATION and access but not the tree. The only source naming the tree, its species and its measurements is the register itself; the matching OSM natural=tree node (id 13092900313) carries reg_ref=672, i.e. it republishes the same register entry rather than confirming it independently, same pattern as the Gran Via palm and the INVASSAT fig in this same file. IMPORTANT: do not confuse this garden with the separate, larger 'Jardi d'Aiora' / Palacete y Jardin de Ayora about 300m away (a Bien de Interes Cultural with its own well documented group of centenarian ficus); a 2019 article about a fallen monumental tree there ('El parque de Ayora olvidado, el ficus caido sigue alli') is about THAT garden, not this one, and does not apply to this candidate. Access looks clean and free (small public garden, no gate or fee found); worth a second pass focused specifically on finding an independent description of this individual tree, e.g. a Valencia city 'ficha arbol monumental' PDF (the naming pattern exists on valencia.es but the one found this pass, for a different id, would not render as text) or local press on this garden's ficus specifically.

leads.name: The Ficus of the Corts Valencianes
leads.why: PULLED FROM THE LIVE PAGE 2026-08-29 on hard rule 10. Inside the working seat of the Valencian regional parliament, visible only on a free guided tour that must be booked in advance, is not offered in August, and which the entry itself called not a walk-up, casual-visit tree. Nothing is wrong with the tree and the research is kept here in full; it can go back the day the access changes. Access as published: RESTRICTED: this is the working seat of the Valencian regional parliament (Corts Valencianes), inside the Palau de Benicarlo / Palau dels Borja. The garden and ficus are visible only on a free guided tour, offered Mondays and Fridays mornings at 10:00/11:00/12:00/13:00, must be booked in advance by phone or the Corts Valencianes website, and NOT offered in August. This is not a walk-up, casual-visit tree.
leads.age_estimate: sources disagree: called both 'century-old' and dated to the second half of the 19th century
leads.story:
One of the largest fig trees in Valencia grows in a garden you can enter twice a week, by appointment, and not at all in August. It stands in the courtyard of the Palau de Benicarlo, also known as the Palau dels Borja, which is the working seat of the Corts Valencianes, the Valencian regional parliament. The only way to stand under it is the free guided tour of the building, offered on Monday and Friday mornings and booked in advance through the parliament itself. The tour runs about an hour and spends most of it on the debating chamber rather than the garden, which is worth knowing before you go.

The tree is in the same weight class as the city's famous ones. The regional register measures its trunk at 13.6 metres around, within centimetres of El Titan in the Parterre. Its age is disputed. One account calls it simply a century old, 22 metres tall with a crown spreading more than 12 metres. Another dates its origins to the second half of the nineteenth century, which would make it something between 127 and 176. Both figures are in circulation and neither has a planting record behind it.

So this is the least casual visit on the list, and the only tree here that requires a phone call. It also spends its life inside a security perimeter, tended by a government that lists it as one of the region's monumental trees.

blocked.name: Ficus del INVASSAT
blocked.reason: RESTRICTED, hard rule 10. Register point sits at Carrer de Valencia 32, Burjassot (confirmed by reverse geocoding and by an OSM natural=tree node, id 13092900332, itself sourced from the same register entry reg_ref=2377, so not counted as an independent source), the address of INVASSAT's Centro Territorial de Valencia, the Generalitat Valenciana's occupational safety and health institute. This is a working government administrative office, not a museum, park or heritage site with public opening hours: INVASSAT's own contact page gives only phone/fax/address, no visitor information, no mention of a garden or public grounds, and nothing found (Burjassot municipal tree ordinance PDF, general web search on the building's history, OSM building/office tagging around the point) establishes a public path or open courtyard reaching the tree. The register itself even names the tree after the institute that occupies the site, which is the same pattern as the already-pulled vlc_012 (Ficus de la Corts Valencianes, inside the working seat of the regional parliament): a genuinely large specimen (11.58m girth, in the same weight class as El Titan and the Corts fig) standing on a government office's own premises rather than on ground the public may walk onto without anyone's permission. Per the three-test rule in hard rule 10 (can they get in without asking anyone's permission; does access read honestly; is it not somebody's workplace/home-equivalent), this fails the first test on the evidence available. Not deleted: if a future pass finds evidence of a public path, opening hours or a guided-visit programme (the CLAUDE.md booking exception), it can be reconsidered exactly like the Corts fig.

blocked.name: Ficus del Palacio de Raga (interior)
blocked.reason: PRIVATE LAND, not open to visitors. Stands inside the walled courtyard of the former Palacio de Raga, which today is a Generalitat Valenciana residencia (RPM Palau de Raga), a social-services care home and day centre for the elderly, not a museum or venue with public opening hours. Local legend holds it is the older and larger of the two Raga-area ficus (a supposed gift from botanist Cavanilles, which if true would put it over 200 years old), but it cannot be visited and its location is inside a residential care facility, which this project does not publish per hard rule 10. The PUBLIC tree 30m away in the same plaza is delivered as vlc_011; do not confuse the two.
